blocks.text: It was now late in the afternoon, and sunset was not far away. We had to accept that our chance had passed. With heavy hearts, we agreed with the Professor when he said:

“Let us go back to Madam Mina—poor, poor dear Madam Mina. We have done everything we can do right now. At least we can protect her there. But we do not need to lose all hope. There is only one more box of earth, and we must try to find it. When that is done, all may still be well.” I could see that he spoke as bravely as he could to comfort Harker. The poor man had quite lost his strength and control. From time to time he gave a low groan that he could not hold back. He was thinking of his wife.

With sad hearts, we came back to my house. There we found Mrs. Harker waiting for us. She looked cheerful in a way that showed her great bravery and unselfish care for others. When she saw our faces, her own face became as pale as death. For a second or two her eyes were closed, as if she were praying silently. Then she said cheerfully:

“I can never thank you all enough. Oh, my poor darling!” As she spoke, she took her husband’s grey head in her hands and kissed it. “Lay your poor head here and rest it. All will still be well, dear! God will protect us if He chooses to do so in His good purpose.” The poor man groaned. His terrible misery was too deep and grand for words.

We had a quick, simple supper together, eaten only because we had to eat. Still, I think it cheered us all up a little. None of us had eaten anything since breakfast. Perhaps it was only the physical warmth that food gives to hungry people. Or perhaps the feeling of being together helped us. In any case, we were all less miserable, and we saw the next day as not completely without hope. As we had promised, we told Mrs. Harker everything that had happened. At times she turned as white as snow when danger had seemed to threaten her husband. At other times her face turned red when his deep love and loyalty toward her became clear. Even so, she listened bravely and calmly. We came to the part where Harker had rushed at the Count so carelessly, without thinking of the danger. Then she held tightly to her husband’s arm, as if holding on to him could protect him from any harm that might come. However, she said nothing until the whole story was told and we had explained everything up to the present moment. Then, without letting go of her husband’s hand, she stood up among us and spoke. I wish I could give any idea of that scene! There stood that sweet, sweet, good, good woman in all the bright beauty of her youth and lively spirit. On her forehead was the red scar. She was aware of it, and we ground our teeth in anger when we saw it, because we remembered where it had come from and how. Her loving kindness stood against our dark, hard hate. Her gentle faith stood against all our fears and doubts. And yet we knew that, as far as outward signs went, she was shut out from God, in spite of all her goodness, purity, and faith.

“Jonathan,” she said. The word sounded like music on her lips because it was so full of love and gentle care. “Jonathan dear, and all of you, my true, true friends, I want you to remember something through all this terrible time. I know that you must fight. I know that you must destroy, just as you destroyed the false Lucy so that the true Lucy could live in the life after death. But it is not a work of hate. That poor soul who has caused all this misery is the saddest case of all. Just think how joyful he will be when the worse part of him is also destroyed, so that his better part may have eternal life of the spirit. You must feel pity for him too, even though that pity must not stop your hands from destroying him.”

As she spoke, I could see her husband’s face grow dark and tighten. It looked as if the strong emotion inside him were drying up his very soul to its center. Without thinking, he held his wife’s hand more and more tightly, until his knuckles looked white. I knew she must have suffered pain from his grip, but she did not pull back or show it. Instead, she looked at him with eyes that begged him more strongly than ever. When she stopped speaking, he jumped to his feet. He almost tore his hand away from hers as he spoke:
